title: Guy Turcotte, who killed his 2 children, denied supervised outing from prison
summary: Guy Turcotte, a Quebec man serving a life sentence for stabbig his two children to death, was denied supervised outings from prison by the Parole Board of Canada on Tuesday.

image.caption: Guy Turcotte leaves the courtroom at the Saint Jérôme courthouse, Dec. 5, 2015, on the sixth day of jury deliberations in his trial. Turcotte was convicted of second-degree murder in the deaths of his two children, Olivier and Anne-Sophie. (Graham Hughes/The Canadian Press)

Former Quebec doctor serving life sentence for stabbing deaths of his children in 2009
Guy Turcotte, a Quebec man serving a life sentence for stabbing his two children to death, was denied supervised outings from prison by the Parole Board of Canada on Tuesday.
Below is a previous version of this story.
A Quebec man found guilty of second-degree murder in the stabbing deaths of his two children is expected to appear today before the Parole Board of Canada.
Guy Turcotte is expected to make a request for temporary escorted absences from prison.
The former cardiologist was found guilty in December 2015 after stabbing his five-year-old son Olivier and his three-year-old daughter Anne-Sophie dozens of times in 2009.
The now 54-year-old was sentenced to life in prison with no possibility of parole for 17 years.

items: Guy Turcotte, who killed his 2 children, requesting temporary absence from prison

blocks.text: Turcotte was originally found not criminally responsible for the murders in 2011, but that verdict was overturned on appeal.
A spokesperson for the Parole Board of Canada says decisions on escorted temporary absence requests are not published, but may be delivered orally at the end of the hearing.
